competitive_landscape: Public marine transport is limited — sightseeing boats, the Big Bus boat tour and private charters (including resort transfers to Sir Bani Yas via Jebel Dhanna). The islands that define Abu Dhabi — Saadiyat, Yas, Lulu, Sir Bani Yas — are stitched together by car and bridge, not by a fast water network. The wildlife and mangrove zones need zero-wake craft that today barely exist.

regulatory_note: Marine mobility sits under the Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) and Abu Dhabi maritime authorities, with marine-protected-area and mangrove rules favouring silent, zero-wake, zero-emission craft. (Authority engagement to be coordinated at leadership level.)
seasonality: Sheltered island and mangrove waters are operable year-round. Summer (Jun–Sep) is hot; winter (Oct–Apr) is the peak window with occasional shamal chop that foiling smooths. Zero-wake all-electric operation suits the protected mangrove reserves in any season.

summary: Abu Dhabi is built across an archipelago: the CBD island, Saadiyat's cultural district, Yas leisure, Lulu, the mangroves and the far wildlife islands. Almost every premium journey wants to be a short water hop, and the outer luxury islands have no fast, clean link at all.
tagline: A capital of islands — culture, leisure and wildlife, all separated by water.
transit_planning: For the integrated transport authority: a premium zero-emission foiling layer connecting the capital's islands and the cultural district, plus a credible decarbonization path for intra-capital marine modes — additive to existing services and uniquely suited to the protected mangrove waters.
